Wesley Jackson
Preserved Primary Document • jacksnw1.htm
Wesley Jackson (also known as William Wesley Jackson)
is my earliest confirmed JACKSON ancestor. According to his grave marker at the St. James Union AME Church, he was born on 11 July,
1811
and he died on 11 March,
1877
. As of now, his parents are unknown.
According to the census records for
1850
/60/70, Wesley was a farmer who lived most of his life in Northwest Fork Hundred in Sussex Co., DE. Northwest Fork is not near the current Indian River community but is, instead, just north of the town of Seaford (and the headwaters of the Nanticoke River) on the Maryland border.
Based on these census records we also know that Wesley's wife was named Elizabeth. The death certificate for her son, William, lists her maiden name as PALMER.
Elizabeth Jackson is buried at the  Indian Mission Church cemetery in Sussex Co. Her grave marker lists her birthdate as 6 January,
1820
and her death date as
6 January 1896
. It is interesting that Elizabeth chose to be buried at Indian Mission cemetery instead of at the St. James Church with her husband. This suggests that Elizabeth (and her family?) may have had close ties to the Indian River community, despite living in Northwest Fork.
Based on the birthdate of their first child, Wesley and Elizabeth were probably married sometime before
1840
.
Wesley and Elizabeth had the following children:
Mary Elizabeth Jackson (c.
1840
- ) married Levi Mosley  on Dec. 30,

Wesley Jackson

Preserved Primary Document • jacksnw1.htm

Wesley Jackson (also known as William Wesley Jackson) is my earliest confirmed JACKSON ancestor. According to his grave marker at the St. James Union AME Church, he was born on 11 July, 1811 and he died on 11 March, 1877. As of now, his parents are unknown. According to the census records for 1850/60/70, Wesley was a farmer who lived most of his life in Northwest Fork Hundred in Sussex Co., DE. Northwest Fork is not near the current Indian River community but is, instead, just north of the town of Seaford (and the headwaters of the Nanticoke River) on the Maryland border. Based on these census records we also know that Wesley's wife was named Elizabeth. The death certificate for her son, William, lists her maiden name as PALMER. Elizabeth Jackson is buried at the Indian Mission Church cemetery in Sussex Co. Her grave marker lists her birthdate as 6 January, 1820 and her death date as 6 January 1896. It is interesting that Elizabeth chose to be buried at Indian Mission cemetery instead of at the St. James Church with her husband. This suggests that Elizabeth (and her family?) may have had close ties to the Indian River community, despite living in Northwest Fork. Based on the birthdate of their first child, Wesley and Elizabeth were probably married sometime before 1840. Wesley and Elizabeth had the following children: Mary Elizabeth Jackson (c. 1840- ) married Levi Mosley on Dec. 30, 1858 Robert B. Jackson (1842-1915) married Lydia Ann Wright James M Jackson (1845 -1926) married Sarah J. Unknown (1856 - 1920) Martha Jackson (c. 1846- ) no information on Martha but the Jackson Bible suggests that she married a "Harmon" and died on 7/10/1895 William W.Jackson (3/1/1848 - 5/17/1925): born possibly in Northwest Fork Hundred, Sussex Co., DE. and appears with his family in the 1850 and 1860 DE. census records but not in the 1870 census so it is possible he was married by then. I have no information on William but see the Jackson Bible . Nathaniel Jackson (1850-1934 ) married Lucy Perkins Catherine Jackson (c. 1856- ) not in the 1860 census Jane Jackson (c. 1857- ) not in the 1870 census John H. Jackson was born 8 January, 1859 in Northwest Fork Hundred, Sussex Co., DE. and appears with his family in the 1860 and 1870 DE. census records. His grave marker at Indian Mission Church lists his death date as 26 March, 1906 when he died " Aged 47 yrs, 2 mos. & 18 days ". I do not know if John ever married. Rebecca Jackson (c.1862- ) married Levin T. Harmon
